title: Exercise related transient abdominal pain (ETAP): leader article
claims: More than 60% of runners report exercise-related transient abdominal pain (ETAP) in the previous year.
In a 14 km community run/walk, 31% of participants reported ETAP, and 42% of those said it affected their performance.

ETAP can occur in any abdominal region but is most common in the mid-abdomen, especially the lateral aspects; severe episodes are sharp or stabbing, while milder episodes are cramping, aching or pulling.
ETAP is most often provoked by repetitive trunk movement, is aggravated by trunk extension, is more common after meals and in younger people, and may be accompanied by shoulder-tip pain.

The traditional explanations of diaphragm ischaemia and traction on the inferior diaphragmatic ligaments have been challenged, and irritation of the parietal peritoneum has been proposed as an alternative mechanism.
Hypertonic or high-energy-density drinks provoke ETAP more than isotonic or hypotonic drinks; a hunched posture increases susceptibility, and palpation near the joint can reproduce the symptoms.
